Travis Walton tells his alien abduction story in a segment of the Joe Rogan Experience, in his own words. In 1975, Walton vanished for five days after his logging crew reported a craft in an Arizona forest. His case became one of the most famous of its kind.

Walton recounts the light, the missing days, and the polygraph fights that followed him for decades. Rogan asks what the attention did to his life and whether he would take it back. Whether a listener believes a word, the segment preserves the man's own telling of a story that never let him go.

Musician and comedian Reggie Watts joins Joe Rogan to muse on UFOs and to share the tale of his own sighting. Watts is known for improvised music and off-beat humor. His show visits tend to roam far and fast.

Watts tells what he saw in the sky and how it has stayed with him since. He and Rogan bat around what the craft could be, from state tech to guests from far stars. The mood stays light even as the topic runs deep. Listeners get a playful mind on a strange tale. The library holds the segment as an archive record.

A social media adviser to President Trump reveals inside details in this Tucker Carlson episode. The adviser discusses the Epstein files, the standoff with Iran, and commentator Mark Levin's advocacy for Israel. Carlson bills the hour as a tell-all from inside Trump's online operation.

The guest explains how the team handles breaking fights and hostile coverage in real time. He shares his view of the pressure campaigns around Iran policy and the Epstein releases. Carlson asks who inside the movement pushes which message and why. Political and curious viewers get an insider spilling on the message wars.
